newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia lists public firms with commercial activities.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia lists public firms with commercial activities.

text.p: Tunisia has listed 41 firms it says are "public firms" owned 100 percent by the state, out of the 202 firms with state's participation in their capital, in an attempt to clarify their status, officials said.
The list, published in the last issue of the Official Gazetta received on Thursday, defines as public firms those producing goods or services sold to the public.

Among them are the country's electricty and gas company STEG, the oil exploration and production company ETAP, the oil refinery STIR, the state's commodities buying body Office du Commerce, the olive oil body Office de l'Huile and the cereals body Office des Cereales.
The list also includes Tunisie-Telecommunications, the tobacco's firms, urban transports companies, and the social security and retirement funds.
Under the new legislation, these firms have an autonomy in their management and carry their activities under a five-year programme they contract with the government.
In addition to these 41 public firms, the government has listed 78 bodies that are called "public establishments" and do not have commercial activities, officials said.
These agencies, such as the Agence for the Promotion of Investments, are considered as extensions of the public administration, officials said.
The remaining 81 firms which have a public participation in their capital out of the total 202 would fall in the status of ordinary limited companies.
